idiom_name: html/template with FuncMap-registered helpers and methods on the view model
implementation_notes: Go's standard library already contains the view engine, so the pattern is absorbed rather than hand-written: helpers are plain functions registered with Template.Funcs (the FuncMap) and called from actions, and any niladic method on the value that dot refers to is callable as .Method, which makes a method set the Go form of a helper object. Use html/template rather than text/template so contextual autoescaping applies to the helper's output. Retrieval stays in the handler or service: a helper that queries the database inside a {{range}} is the classic Go rendering bug. A helper type with several methods over shared configuration is the justified classic form; for a single formatting rule a plain function is the whole helper.
pitfalls: Functions must be registered before Parse (or via Funcs on the parsed template); an unregistered name is a parse error, while a niladic method that panics or returns an error surfaces only when the action executes.
text/template performs no escaping, so using it for HTML re-opens injection; html/template additionally refuses html/urlquery helpers whose output it cannot verify.
A FuncMap value must be a function of one or two return values with an optional trailing error; a helper returning only an error, or a method that takes arguments, cannot be called from an action.
Executing one *template.Template concurrently is safe, but mutating it (Funcs, Delims) after first use races with rendering.
